1 --- 2 name: mermaidjs-v11 3 description: Create diagrams and visualizations using Mermaid.js v11 syntax. Use when generating flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, state diagrams, ER diagrams, Gantt charts, user journeys, timelines, architecture diagrams, or any of 24+ diagram types. Supports JavaScript API integration, CLI rendering to SVG/PNG/PDF, theming, configuration, and accessibility features. Essential for documentation, technical diagrams, project planning, system architecture, and visual communication. 4 --- 5 6 # Mermaid.js v11 7 8 ## Overview 9 10 Create text-based diagrams using Mermaid.js v11 declarative syntax. Convert code to SVG/PNG/PDF via CLI or render in browsers/markdown files. 11 12 ## Quick Start 13 14 **Basic Diagram Structure:** 15 ``` 16 {diagram-type} 17 {diagram-content} 18 ``` 19 20 **Common Diagram Types:** 21 - `flowchart` - Process flows, decision trees 22 - `sequenceDiagram` - Actor interactions, API flows 23 - `classDiagram` - OOP structures, data models 24 - `stateDiagram` - State machines, workflows 25 - `erDiagram` - Database relationships 26 - `gantt` - Project timelines 27 - `journey` - User experience flows 28 29 See `references/diagram-types.md` for all 24+ types with syntax. 30 31 ## Creating Diagrams 32 33 **Inline Markdown Code Blocks:** 34 ````markdown 35 ```mermaid 36 flowchart TD 37 A[Start] --> B{Decision} 38 B -->|Yes| C[Action] 39 B -->|No| D[End] 40 ``` 41 ```` 42 43 **Configuration via Frontmatter:** 44 ````markdown 45 ```mermaid 46 --- 47 theme: dark 48 --- 49 flowchart LR 50 A --> B 51 ``` 52 ```` 53 54 **Comments:** Use `%% ` prefix for single-line comments. 55 56 ## CLI Usage 57 58 Convert `.mmd` files to images: 59 ```bash 60 # Installation 61 npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 62 63 # Basic conversion 64 mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o diagram.svg 65 66 # With theme and background 67 mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png -t dark -b transparent 68 69 # Custom styling 70 mmdc -i diagram.mmd --cssFile style.css -o output.svg 71 ``` 72 73 See `references/cli-usage.md` for Docker, batch processing, and advanced workflows. 74 75 ## JavaScript Integration 76 77 **HTML Embedding:** 78 ```html 79 
    80	  flowchart TD
    81	    A[Client] --> B[Server]
    82
83 84 85 ``` 86 87 See `references/integration.md` for Node.js API and advanced integration patterns. 88 89 ## Configuration & Theming 90 91 **Common Options:** 92 - `theme`: "default", "dark", "forest", "neutral", "base" 93 - `look`: "classic", "handDrawn" 94 - `fontFamily`: Custom font specification 95 - `securityLevel`: "strict", "loose", "antiscript" 96 97 See `references/configuration.md` for complete config options, theming, and customization. 98 99 ## Practical Patterns 100 101 Load `references/examples.md` for: 102 - Architecture diagrams 103 - API documentation flows 104 - Database schemas 105 - Project timelines 106 - State machines 107 - User journey maps 108 109 ## Resources 110 111 - `references/diagram-types.md` - Syntax for all 24+ diagram types 112 - `references/configuration.md` - Config, theming, accessibility 113 - `references/cli-usage.md` - CLI commands and workflows 114 - `references/integration.md` - JavaScript API and embedding 115 - `references/examples.md` - Practical patterns and use cases

     4	Four datasets capture the transmission of US monetary tightening to eight emerging-market economies (Turkey, Argentina, Egypt, South Africa, Brazil, Pakistan, Ghana, Sri Lanka) across four dimensions: US interest rates, external debt burdens, currency depreciation, and sovereign credit rating actions.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### fed_funds_rate
     9	Quarterly upper-bound Fed Funds rate from Q4 2021 to Q4 2024. Fields: `date` (YYYY-QN string), `rate_pct` (float, percent). 13 rows.
    10	
    11	### external_debt_to_gdp
    12	Annual external-debt-to-GDP ratios for 8 countries, 2021–2024. Fields: `country` (string), `year` (int), `debt_gdp_pct` (float, percent of GDP). 32 rows.
    13	
    14	### currency_depreciation
    15	Cumulative local-currency depreciation against the USD from a January 2021 baseline, measured at year-end. Fields: `country` (string), `year` (int), `depreciation_pct` (float, positive = weaker). 32 rows.
    16	
    17	### sovereign_rating_changes
    18	Composite sovereign credit rating actions from major agencies. Fields: `country` (string), `date` (YYYY-MM string), `action` (enum: affirm, downgrade, upgrade, default), `rating_level` (string, S&P-style notation). 31 rows.
    19	
    20	## Data Notes
    21	- Rating levels are simplified composites and may not exactly match any single agency's scale.
    22	- Currency depreciation is cumulative from Jan 2021, not year-over-year.
    23	- Sri Lanka and Ghana entered selective default during the observation period.
    24	- External debt figures are estimates rounded to one decimal place.

1	# Mermaid.js Diagram Types
     2	
     3	Comprehensive syntax reference for all 24+ diagram types in Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Core Diagrams
     6	
     7	### Flowchart
     8	Process flows, decision trees, workflows.
     9	
    10	**Syntax:**
    11	```
    12	flowchart {direction}
    13	  {nodeId}[{label}] {arrow} {nodeId}[{label}]
    14	```
    15	
    16	**Directions:** TB/TD (top-bottom), BT, LR (left-right), RL
    17	**Shapes:** `()` round, `[]` rect, `{}` diamond, `{{}}` hexagon, `(())` circle
    18	**Arrows:** `-->` solid, `-.->` dotted, `==>` thick
    19	**Subgraphs:** Group related nodes
    20	
    21	### Sequence Diagram
    22	Actor interactions, API flows, message sequences.
    23	
    24	**Syntax:**
    25	```
    26	sequenceDiagram
    27	  participant A as Actor
    28	  A->>B: Message
    29	  activate B
    30	  B-->>A: Response
    31	  deactivate B
    32	```
    33	
    34	**Arrows:** `->` solid, `->>` arrow, `-->` dotted, `-x` cross, `-)` async
    35	**Features:** Loops, alternatives, parallel, optional, critical regions
    36	
    37	### Class Diagram
    38	OOP structures, inheritance, relationships.
    39	
    40	**Syntax:**
    41	```
    42	classDiagram
    43	  class Animal {
    44	    +String name
    45	    -int age
    46	    +void eat()
    47	  }
    48	  Animal <|-- Dog : inherits
    49	```
    50	
    51	**Visibility:** `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected, `~` package
    52	**Relationships:** `<|--` inheritance, `*--` composition, `o--` aggregation, `-->` association
    53	
    54	### State Diagram
    55	State machines, transitions, workflows.
    56	
    57	**Syntax:**

    76	
    77	**Cardinality:** `||` one, `|o` zero-one, `}|` one-many, `}o` zero-many

"""
Generate a publication-ready faceted chart showing Fed rate transmission
to 8 emerging markets: external debt, currency depreciation, and rating actions.
"""
import json
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

fed = data['fed_funds_rate']['data']
debt = data['external_debt_to_gdp']['data']
dep = data['currency_depreciation']['data']
ratings = data['sovereign_rating_changes']['data']

# Country order: sort by 2024 debt-to-GDP descending for narrative flow
countries = sorted(
    list(set(d['country'] for d in debt)),
    key=lambda c: next(d['debt_gdp_pct'] for d in debt if d['country'] == c and d['year'] == 2024),
    reverse=True
)

# Time mapping: Q4 2021 = 0, Q1 2022 = 1, ..., Q4 2024 = 12
quarters = [f"{y}-Q{q}" for y in range(2021, 2025) for q in range(1, 5)]
quarter_map = {q: i for i, q in enumerate(quarters)}
base_q = quarter_map['2021-Q4']

def date_to_x(date_str):
    """Convert YYYY-QN or YYYY-MM to x-coordinate."""
    if '-Q' in date_str:
        return quarter_map[date_str] - base_q
    else:
        y, m = map(int, date_str.split('-'))
        q = (m - 1) // 3 + 1
        q_str = f"{y}-Q{q}"
        return quarter_map.get(q_str, 0) - base_q

fed_x = [date_to_x(d['date']) for d in fed]
fed_y = [d['rate_pct'] for d in fed]

# Figure setup: editorial style
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.sans-serif': ['DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica'],
    'axes.edgecolor': '#333333',
    'axes.labelcolor': '#333333',
    'xtick.color': '#333333',
    'ytick.color': '#333333',
    'text.color': '#333333',
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.alpha': 0.3,
    'grid.color': '#cccccc',
    'figure.facecolor': 'white',
    'axes.facecolor': 'white',
})

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(14, 16), sharex=True, sharey=False)
fig.subplots_adjust(hspace=0.35, wspace=0.25, left=0.08, right=0.92, top=0.92, bottom=0.06)

# Colors
COLOR_DEBT = '#1f5a8c'      # Steel blue
COLOR_DEP = '#c44e52'       # Muted red
COLOR_FED = '#4a4a4a'       # Dark gray
COLOR_UPGRADE = '#2ca02c'
COLOR_DOWNGRADE = '#d62728'
COLOR_AFFIRM = '#7f7f7f'
COLOR_DEFAULT = '#000000'

# Rating action symbols
SYMBOLS = {
    'upgrade': '▲',
    'downgrade': '▼',
    'affirm': '●',
    'default': '✕'
}
COLORS_RATING = {
    'upgrade': COLOR_UPGRADE,
    'downgrade': COLOR_DOWNGRADE,
    'affirm': COLOR_AFFIRM,
    'default': COLOR_DEFAULT,
}

# Fed rate line for legend
fed_line = Line2D([0], [0], color=COLOR_FED, linewidth=1.5, linestyle='--', label='Fed Funds Rate (%)')

for idx, country in enumerate(countries):
    ax = axes[idx // 2, idx % 2]
    ax2 = ax.twinx()
    
    # Only show right y-axis label on right column
    if idx % 2 == 1:
        ax2.set_ylabel('Fed Funds Rate (%)', fontsize=9, color=COLOR_FED, fontweight='bold')
        ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=COLOR_FED, labelsize=8)
    else:
        ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=COLOR_FED, labelsize=8)
    
    # Country debt and depreciation data
    c_debt = sorted([d for d in debt if d['country'] == country], key=lambda x: x['year'])
    c_dep = sorted([d for d in dep if d['country'] == country], key=lambda x: x['year'])
    
    debt_x = [date_to_x(f"{d['year']}-Q4") for d in c_debt]
    debt_y = [d['debt_gdp_pct'] for d in c_debt]
    dep_x = [date_to_x(f"{d['year']}-Q4") for d in c_dep]
    dep_y = [d['depreciation_pct'] for d in c_dep]
    
    # Bars for debt-to-GDP (width ~1.5 quarters)
    bar_width = 1.2
    bars = ax.bar(debt_x, debt_y, width=bar_width, color=COLOR_DEBT, alpha=0.7, label='External Debt / GDP (%)', zorder=3)
    
    # Line for currency depreciation
    line_dep, = ax.plot(dep_x, dep_y, color=COLOR_DEP, linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Currency Depreciation (%)', zorder=4)
    
    # Fed funds rate on secondary axis
    ax2.plot(fed_x, fed_y, color=COLOR_FED, linewidth=1.5, linestyle='--', alpha=0.8, zorder=2)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 6.5)
    
    # Primary axis
    ax.set_ylim(0, 105)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 12.5)
    if idx >= 6:
        ax.set_xticks(range(0, 13, 2))
        ax.set_xticklabels(['Q4\n2021', 'Q2\n2022', 'Q4\n2022', 'Q2\n2023', 'Q4\n2023', 'Q2\n2024', 'Q4\n2024'], fontsize=8)
    else:
        ax.set_xticks(range(0, 13, 2))
    
    if idx % 2 == 0:
        ax.set_ylabel('Percent', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')
    
    # Country title
    ax.set_title(country, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=8, color='#1a1a1a')
    
    # Rating actions
    c_ratings = [r for r in ratings if r['country'] == country]
    for r in c_ratings:
        rx = date_to_x(r['date'])
        if rx < -0.5:
            rx = -0.3
        action = r['action']
        sym = SYMBOLS[action]
        col = COLORS_RATING[action]
        # Place symbols near top
        y_pos = 92 + (hash(r['date']) % 10)  # slight jitter to avoid overlap
        ax.annotate(sym, (rx, 95), fontsize=11, color=col, ha='center', va='center', fontweight='bold', zorder=5)
        ax.annotate(r['rating_level'], (rx, 90), fontsize=7, color=col, ha='center', va='top', fontweight='bold', zorder=5)
    
    # Shade steep-hike period (Q1 2022 to Q3 2023)
    ax.axvspan(date_to_x('2022-Q1'), date_to_x('2023-Q3'), color=COLOR_FED, alpha=0.04, zorder=1)

# Add legends
# Make a combined legend below the chart
legend_elements = [
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=COLOR_DEBT, alpha=0.7, label='External Debt to GDP (%)'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=COLOR_DEP, linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Currency Depreciation (%)'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=COLOR_FED, linewidth=1.5, linestyle='--', label='Fed Funds Rate (%)'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='▼', color='w', markerfacecolor=COLOR_DOWNGRADE, markersize=10, label='Downgrade'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='▲', color='w', markerfacecolor=COLOR_UPGRADE, markersize=10, label='Upgrade'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='●', color='w', markerfacecolor=COLOR_AFFIRM, markersize=9, label='Affirm'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='✕', color='w', markerfacecolor=COLOR_DEFAULT, markersize=9, label='Default'),
]
fig.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower center', ncol=4, fontsize=9,
           frameon=True, fancybox=False, edgecolor='#cccccc', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.01))

# Main title
fig.suptitle('Fed Rate Transmission to Emerging Markets (2021–2024)\nExternal Debt, Currency Depreciation, and Sovereign Rating Actions',
             fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', y=0.97, color='#1a1a1a')

# Subtitle / annotation
fig.text(0.5, 0.935, 'Shaded background indicates the steep Fed hiking phase (Q1 2022 – Q3 2023)',
         ha='center', fontsize=9, style='italic', color='#555555')

# Save
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white', edgecolor='none')
print("Saved /app/output/result.png")
